```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lmtest)
library(estimatr)
library(ggthemes)
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)
library(stargazer)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(car) # For Levene's test
library(stats)
library(pwr) # For sample size calculation
library(corrplot)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)       # For regression summary
library(modelsummary) # For table summary
library(ggpubr)      # To combine multiple plots
library(car)         # For Levene's Test
library(knitr)       # For output tables
library(kableExtra)  # Enhanced tables
```

```{r}
# Load datasets (replace with your file paths)
test_group <- read.csv("test_group.csv")
control_group <- read.csv("control_group.csv")
```

```{r}
# Combine datasets
data <- bind_rows(
  test_group %>% mutate(Group = "Test"),
  control_group %>% mutate(Group = "Control")
)
```

```{r}
# Check structure
str(data)
summary(data)
```

```{r}
# Convert Group to Factor
data$Group <- as.factor(data$Group)
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Pre-Analysis Steps
# --------------------------
# A. Sample Size Calculation
# Define inputs
baseline_conversion_rate <- mean(control_group$Click / control_group$Purchase, na.rm = TRUE)  # Example metric
minimum_detectable_effect <- 0.20  # Define MDE as a proportion (e.g., 5%)
power <- 0.8
alpha <- 0.05
```

```{r}
# Calculate effect size for proportion test
effect_size <- ES.h(baseline_conversion_rate, baseline_conversion_rate + minimum_detectable_effect)
```

```{r}
# Calculate required sample size
sample_size <- pwr.2p.test(h = effect_size, sig.level = alpha, power = power, alternative = "two.sided")
print(sample_size)
```

```{r}
# Check if current data meets sample size requirements
actual_sample_size <- data %>% group_by(Group) %>% summarise(n = n())
print(actual_sample_size)
```

```{r}
# B. Randomization Validity (A/A Test)
control_split <- control_group %>%
  mutate(Split = sample(c("Group1", "Group2"), size = n(), replace = TRUE))

aa_test <- t.test(Purchase ~ Split, data = control_split)
print(aa_test)
```

```{r}
# Step 2: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA)
# ---------------------------------------
# A. Data Cleaning
# Handle missing values
data <- data %>% drop_na()
```

```{r}
# Normalize metrics (e.g., Clicks per 1,000 Impressions)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    Normalized_Clicks = Click / Impression * 1000,
    Normalized_Purchase = Purchase / Impression * 1000
  )
```

```{r}
# B. Descriptive Statistics
summary_stats <- data %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_Earning = mean(Earning, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_Earning = sd(Earning, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_Earning = median(Earning, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_Earning = min(Earning, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_Earning = max(Earning, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(summary_stats)
```

```{r}
# Step 8: Parallel Time Series Graph for Earnings
# -----------------------------------------------

# Simulate Day Column from 1 to 40
data$Day <- rep(1:40, length.out = nrow(data))

# Aggregate Mean Earnings by Day and Group
time_series <- data %>%
  group_by(Day, Group) %>%
  summarise(Mean_Earning = mean(Earning, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Split the data for Control and Test Groups
control_data <- time_series %>% filter(Group == "Control")
test_data <- time_series %>% filter(Group == "Test")

# Plot Side-by-Side Time Series for Control and Test Groups
p1 <- ggplot(control_data, aes(x = Day, y = Mean_Earning)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Control Group", x = "Day", y = "Mean Earnings") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(test_data, aes(x = Day, y = Mean_Earning)) +
  geom_line(color = "red", size = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Test Group", x = "Day", y = "Mean Earnings") +
  theme_minimal()

# Combine Both Plots Side-by-Side
library(ggpubr)
ggarrange(p1, p2, ncol = 1, nrow = 2)
```

```{r}
# Calculate group means
mean_control <- mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_test <- mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)

# Add the lift line across the two means
ggplot(data, aes(x = Earning, fill = Group, color = Group)) +
  # Histogram
  geom_histogram(position = "identity", bins = 30, alpha = 0.5) +
  # Density Plot
  geom_density(aes(y = ..scaled.. * 20), alpha = 0.7) +
  # Add a line to represent the lift
  geom_segment(aes(x = mean_control, xend = mean_test, 
                   y = 10, yend = 10),  # Adjust y-position for visibility
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")), 
               color = "black", size = 1) +
  # Add text for clarity
  annotate("text", x = (mean_control + mean_test) / 2, y = 15, 
           label = paste0("Lift: ", round(((mean_test - mean_control) / mean_control) * 100, 2), "%"), 
           color = "black", size = 4) +
  # Labels and theme
  labs(title = "Earnings Histogram and Density by Group with Lift",
       x = "Earnings", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Calculate group means
mean_control_impression <- mean(data$Impression[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_test_impression <- mean(data$Impression[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)

# Add the lift line across the two means
ggplot(data, aes(x = Impression, fill = Group, color = Group)) +
  # Density Plot
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4, adjust = 1.2) + # Smoother density
  # Add a line to represent the lift
  geom_segment(aes(x = mean_control_impression, xend = mean_test_impression, 
                   y = 0.01, yend = 0.01),  # Adjust y-position for visibility
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm")), 
               color = "black", size = 1) +
  # Add text for clarity
  annotate("text", x = (mean_control_impression + mean_test_impression) / 2, y = 0.015, 
           label = paste0("Lift: ", round(((mean_test_impression - mean_control_impression) / mean_control_impression) * 100, 2), "%"), 
           color = "black", size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  # Add vertical lines at the group means
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_control_impression, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_test_impression, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
  # Labels and theme
  labs(title = "Impressions Density by Group with Lift",
       x = "Impressions", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Linear regression with Group, Clicks, and Impressions
lm1 <- lm(Earning ~ Group + Click + Impression, data = data)

# Display regression summary
summary(lm1)

# Linear regression with interaction between Group and Clicks
lm2 <- lm(Earning ~ Group * Click + Impression, data = data)

# Display regression summary
summary(lm2)

# Plot residuals to check for normality and heteroskedasticity
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  # Multiple plots
plot(lm1)  # Diagnostics for the first model
plot(lm2)  # Diagnostics for the second model

# Compare models using ANOVA
anova(lm1, lm2)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(tibble)  # For tabulated results
library(kableExtra)  # For formatted tables

# Linear regression with Group, Clicks, and Impressions
lm1 <- lm(Earning ~ Group + Click + Impression, data = data)
summary_lm1 <- summary(lm1)

# Linear regression with interaction between Group and Clicks
lm2 <- lm(Earning ~ Group * Click + Impression, data = data)
summary_lm2 <- summary(lm2)

# Tabulated summary of key regression coefficients
regression_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Term = c("(Intercept)", "Group (Test)", "Click", "Impression", "Group (Test):Click"),
  Estimate_Model1 = c(summary_lm1$coefficients[1:4, "Estimate"], NA),
  p_value_Model1 = c(summary_lm1$coefficients[1:4, "Pr(>|t|)"], NA),
  Estimate_Model2 = c(summary_lm2$coefficients[1:5, "Estimate"]),
  p_value_Model2 = c(summary_lm2$coefficients[1:5, "Pr(>|t|)"])
)

# Print a formatted table for presentation
regression_table %>%
  kbl(caption = "Regression Model Comparison: With and Without Interaction") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12)

# Compare models using ANOVA
anova_result <- anova(lm1, lm2)

# Print ANOVA results
print("ANOVA Comparison Between Models:")
print(anova_result)

# Plot residuals to check for normality and heteroskedasticity
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  # Multiple plots
plot(lm1, main = "Model 1 Diagnostics")  # Diagnostics for the first model
plot(lm2, main = "Model 2 Diagnostics")  # Diagnostics for the second model
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(stargazer)   # For nicely formatted regression tables
library(tibble)      # For additional tabulated results
library(kableExtra)  # For enhanced table output

# Linear regression with Group, Clicks, and Impressions
lm1 <- lm(Earning ~ Group + Click + Impression, data = data)

# Linear regression with interaction between Group and Clicks
lm2 <- lm(Earning ~ Group * Click + Impression, data = data)

# 1. Tabulate Regression Results with Stargazer
stargazer(lm1, lm2, 
          type = "text", 
          title = "Regression Model Comparison: With and Without Interaction", 
          dep.var.labels = "Earnings", 
          covariate.labels = c("(Intercept)", "Group (Test)", "Click", "Impression", "Group (Test):Click"),
          out = "regression_table.txt")  # Outputs to console and saves as a .txt file

# 2. Tabulate ANOVA Results Separately
anova_result <- anova(lm1, lm2)

# Convert ANOVA results into a neat table for presentation
anova_table <- tibble::tibble(
  Model = c("Model 1", "Model 2"),
  Res.Df = anova_result$Res.Df,
  RSS = round(anova_result$RSS, 2),
  Sum_of_Squares = c(NA, round(diff(anova_result$RSS), 2)),
  F_statistic = c(NA, round(anova_result$F[2], 2)),
  p_value = c(NA, round(anova_result$`Pr(>F)`[2], 4))
)

# Display ANOVA table
anova_table %>%
  kbl(caption = "ANOVA Comparison Between Models") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12)

# 3. Plot residuals to check for normality and heteroskedasticity
par(mfrow = c(2, 2))  # Multiple plots
plot(lm1, main = "Model 1 Diagnostics")  # Diagnostics for the first model
plot(lm2, main = "Model 2 Diagnostics")  # Diagnostics for the second model

```

```{r}
# Step 3: Assumption Checks for Parametric Tests
# ----------------------------------------------
# A. Test for Normality
shapiro_test <- data %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(p_value = shapiro.test(Earning)$p.value)
print(shapiro_test)
```

```{r}
# Step 3: Assumption Checks for Parametric Tests
# A. Test for Normality
shapiro_test <- data %>%
  group_by(Group) %>%
  summarise(p_value = shapiro.test(Earning)$p.value)

# Tabulate Results
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Format and display the table
shapiro_test %>%
  mutate(Normality = ifelse(p_value > 0.05, "Assumption Met", "Assumption Violated")) %>%
  kable("html", caption = "Shapiro-Wilk Test for Normality of Earnings by Group") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive")) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE) %>%
  column_spec(2, color = "blue") %>%
  column_spec(3, bold = TRUE, color = ifelse(shapiro_test$p_value > 0.05, "green", "red")) 

```

```{r}
# B. Test for Homogeneity of Variance
levene_test <- leveneTest(Earning ~ Group, data = data)
print(levene_test)
```

```{r}
# Step 4: Hypothesis Testing
# --------------------------
# A. Chi-Square Test
impressions_table <- table(data$Group, data$Impression > 0)
chi_sq_test <- chisq.test(impressions_table)
print(chi_sq_test)
```

```{r}
# B. Two-Sample t-Test
if (levene_test$`Pr(>F)`[1] > 0.05) {
  t_test <- t.test(Earning ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = TRUE)
} else {
  t_test <- t.test(Earning ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = FALSE)
}
print(t_test)
```

```{r}
# Extract Results for Summary Table with Lift Calculation
results_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric      = c("Earnings", "Purchases", "Clicks"),
  Control     = c(mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  Test        = c(mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  Lift        = c(
    (mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    
    (mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    
    (mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ),
  p_value     = c(t_test$p.value, t_test_purchase$p.value, t_test_click$p.value)
)

# Print Summary Table
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

kable(results_summary, caption = "Summary of T-Test Results with Lift for Key Metrics") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) # Bold the header row
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(car)          # For Levene's Test
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Step 1: Perform Levene's Test and T-tests for Earnings, Purchases, and Clicks
# Earnings T-test
if (leveneTest(Earning ~ Group, data = data)$`Pr(>F)`[1] > 0.05) {
  t_test_earning <- t.test(Earning ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = TRUE)
} else {
  t_test_earning <- t.test(Earning ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = FALSE)
}

# Purchases T-test
if (leveneTest(Purchase ~ Group, data = data)$`Pr(>F)`[1] > 0.05) {
  t_test_purchase <- t.test(Purchase ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = TRUE)
} else {
  t_test_purchase <- t.test(Purchase ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = FALSE)
}

# Clicks T-test
if (leveneTest(Click ~ Group, data = data)$`Pr(>F)`[1] > 0.05) {
  t_test_click <- t.test(Click ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = TRUE)
} else {
  t_test_click <- t.test(Click ~ Group, data = data, var.equal = FALSE)
}

# Step 2: Calculate Means, Lift, and Additional T-Test Statistics
results_summary <- data.frame(
  Metric      = c("Earnings", "Purchases", "Clicks"),
  Control     = c(mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  Test        = c(mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)),
  Lift        = c(
    (mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    
    (mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Purchase[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    
    (mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE) - 
     mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)) / 
     mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ),
  t_statistic = c(t_test_earning$statistic, t_test_purchase$statistic, t_test_click$statistic),
  Lower_CI    = c(t_test_earning$conf.int[1], t_test_purchase$conf.int[1], t_test_click$conf.int[1]),
  Upper_CI    = c(t_test_earning$conf.int[2], t_test_purchase$conf.int[2], t_test_click$conf.int[2]),
  p_value     = c(t_test_earning$p.value, t_test_purchase$p.value, t_test_click$p.value)
)

# Step 3: Create a Beautiful Table with knitr
kable(results_summary, 
      caption = "T-Test Results: Control (Maximum Bidding) vs. Test (Average Bidding) Groups") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12) %>%
  column_spec(2:4, width = "3cm") %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, background = "#D3D3D3")
```

```{r}
# Step: Extract Results for Coefficient Plot Correctly
coefficients_data <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Earnings", "Purchases", "Clicks"),
  Estimate = c(
    t_test$estimate[1] - t_test$estimate[2],  # Difference in means for Earnings
    t_test_purchase$estimate[1] - t_test_purchase$estimate[2],  # For Purchases
    t_test_click$estimate[1] - t_test_click$estimate[2]  # For Clicks
  ),
  Lower_CI = c(
    t_test$conf.int[1],       # Confidence interval for Earnings difference
    t_test_purchase$conf.int[1],  # For Purchases
    t_test_click$conf.int[1]      # For Clicks
  ),
  Upper_CI = c(
    t_test$conf.int[2],       # Confidence interval for Earnings difference
    t_test_purchase$conf.int[2],  # For Purchases
    t_test_click$conf.int[2]      # For Clicks
  )
)

# Plot the Coefficient Plot
ggplot(coefficients_data, aes(x = Metric, y = Estimate)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "blue") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Lower_CI, ymax = Upper_CI), width = 0.2, color = "blue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Coefficient Plot: Mean Differences with Confidence Intervals",
    x = "Metric",
    y = "Difference in Means (Test - Control)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r}
# C. ANOVA (Bivariate Analysis)
anova_test <- aov(Earning ~ Group * Normalized_Clicks, data = data)
summary(anova_test)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary libraries
library(broom)        # To tidy the ANOVA results
library(knitr)        # For tabular output
library(kableExtra)   # For enhanced table styling
library(dplyr)        # For data manipulation

# Perform ANOVA test
anova_test <- aov(Earning ~ Group * Normalized_Clicks, data = data)

# Extract and tidy the ANOVA summary
anova_summary <- tidy(summary(anova_test)[[1]])

# Add significance stars based on p-value thresholds
anova_summary <- anova_summary %>%
  mutate(
    Significance = case_when(
      p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
      p.value < 0.01  ~ "**",
      p.value < 0.05  ~ "*",
      TRUE            ~ ""
    )
  )

# Rename columns for better readability
anova_table <- anova_summary %>%
  rename(
    `Source of Variation` = term,
    `Degrees of Freedom` = df,
    `Sum of Squares` = sumsq,
    `Mean Square` = meansq,
    `F-Statistic` = statistic,
    `P-Value` = p.value
  )

# Present the results in a clean table format
kbl(anova_table, caption = "ANOVA Results: Group and Normalized Clicks Interaction Effect",
    digits = 4, align = "c") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)

```

```{r}
# Step 5: Additional Tests
# ------------------------
# A. Effect Size
effect_size <- (mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"]) - mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"])) /
  sd(data$Earning)
print(paste("Effect size (Cohen's d):", effect_size))
```

```{r}
# Calculate group means and standard deviations for Earnings and Clicks
mean_control_earning <- mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_test_earning <- mean(data$Earning[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)
sd_earning <- sd(data$Earning, na.rm = TRUE)

mean_control_click <- mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Control"], na.rm = TRUE)
mean_test_click <- mean(data$Click[data$Group == "Test"], na.rm = TRUE)
sd_click <- sd(data$Click, na.rm = TRUE)

# Calculate Cohen's d for Earnings and Clicks
effect_size_earning <- (mean_test_earning - mean_control_earning) / sd_earning
effect_size_click <- (mean_test_click - mean_control_click) / sd_click

# Create a summary table for effect sizes
effect_size_table <- data.frame(
  Metric           = c("Earnings", "Clicks"),
  Control_Mean     = c(mean_control_earning, mean_control_click),
  Test_Mean        = c(mean_test_earning, mean_test_click),
  Pooled_SD        = c(sd_earning, sd_click),
  Effect_Size_d    = c(effect_size_earning, effect_size_click)
)

# Display the table with formatted output
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

kbl(effect_size_table, 
    caption = "Effect Size (Cohen's d) for Earnings and Clicks", 
    digits = 4, align = "c") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, position = "center", font_size = 12) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
print(paste("Lift in Earning (%):", lift_earning))
```

```{r}
# Visualize the Correlation Matrix with correlation index and color-filled cells
corrplot(
  cor_matrix, 
  method = "color",           # Fill the cells with colors
  type = "upper",             # Display the upper triangle only
  addCoef.col = "black",      # Add correlation coefficients in black
  tl.col = "black",           # Text label color
  tl.srt = 45,                # Rotate text labels
  number.cex = 0.8,           # Size of the correlation index
  col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(200), # Gradient from blue to red
  title = "Correlation Matrix", # Title of the plot
  mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0)         # Margins to accommodate the title
)
```
